headline: US-Iran conflict escalates with naval strikes as MSFT and GOOG slip last night, while the ASX held relatively steady today and OpenAI drops GPT-6 Astra.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft shed 2% last night in a soft session for tech on the NASDAQ. No specific company news drove it — the broader market was cautious, likely linked to geopolitical jitters around the US-Iran conflict and general end-of-week position trimming. The long-term investment case remains solid.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 2.1% today to close at $5.09. No fresh company news, but lithium stocks remain under persistent pressure as global lithium prices stay soft and demand signals from the EV sector are mixed. This one continues to test patience.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped about 1.1% last night. Motley Fool flagged that Alphabet's recent earnings beat was partly inflated by a $77.1 billion unrealised gain on equity holdings — meaning the underlying operating business grew more modestly than the headline numbers suggested. Markets are digesting that nuance.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI bounced 1.6% today to close at $16.44 — a nice recovery session. AI sentiment got a boost from OpenAI dropping GPT-6 Astra today, keeping enthusiasm alive for AI-exposed stocks. Still down about 13% from cost, but the trend today was encouraging.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up 0.4% today to $529.04, nudging further into positive territory overall. The ASX-listed US market ETF benefited from a stable AUD and steady global sentiment heading into the weekend.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG ticked up a modest 0.2% today — quiet but steady. As a diversified multi-asset fund it absorbed the day's mixed signals well. Nothing to worry about here.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up 0.1% today. Emerging markets are broadly stable but caught between geopolitical tension in the Middle East and China's ongoing economic recovery story. Slight positive today is fine.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two crept up 0.3% last night — essentially flat. No specific news. The stock remains underwater overall (-7.5% on your position) as markets wait for GTA VI and other major title catalysts to materialise.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Pilbara keeps bleeding
watch_today.detail: Pilbara closed at $5.09 today, down another 2.1%. You're now sitting on a -24.5% loss on this position. The lithium market remains structurally weak with no near-term catalyst visible. For a long-term holder, the question is whether the thesis (lithium demand from EVs) still holds over 5+ years — it probably does, but this will test conviction. No reason to sell at the bottom, but be clear-eyed about what you're holding.

watch_today.title: MSFT — solid dip, long-term story unchanged
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2% last night to $499.70. Nothing structural has changed — this is noise after a strong run. The Azure AI business, Copilot rollout, and cloud growth story are all intact. For a long-term holder this is not a concern. If you've been thinking about topping up, it's a slightly better entry point than last week.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — good bounce today, AI sentiment lifting
watch_today.detail: GXAI rose 1.6% today and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra launch is keeping AI hype alive. You're still down ~13% on this position overall, but today's move is a reminder of how quickly sentiment can turn. Hold and let the AI thematic play out — this is exactly the kind of ETF built for a multi-year view.

watch_today.title: US-Iran conflict — oil and markets to watch this week
watch_today.detail: The US struck Iranian oil tankers over the weekend in what the AFR called a 'dangerous war escalation'. Oil (WTI) is already at $91.48 a barrel and could spike further if the conflict widens. Higher oil = higher inflation = slower rate cuts globally. Keep an eye on this — it could rattle US markets when they open tonight.

watch_today.title: OpenAI drops GPT-6 Astra today
watch_today.detail: OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra overnight — a new-generation model. Good tailwind for your GXAI.AX holding and the broader AI thematic. Worth knowing about but no action needed.

watch_today.title: RBA rate outlook shifting — watch your mortgage and cash position
watch_today.detail: New reporting suggests Australia is heading into a new interest rate reality, with the RBA flagging rent-driven inflation as a persistent problem. Rate cuts may come later than hoped. If you hold cash or have a mortgage, this is worth keeping in mind over the coming months.

world.summary: The big story this weekend is the US-Iran conflict escalating into direct naval strikes, with Trump hinting at a much bigger Middle East plan. Meanwhile, a US court battle over mail-in voting rules is heating up ahead of the midterms.

stories.title: US strikes Iran's oil tankers — conflict escalates dangerously
stories.why_it_matters: The US military directly struck Iranian oil tankers over the weekend in what analysts are calling a serious escalation of the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Iran has reportedly retaliated with its own attacks on ships in the region. Oil prices were already elevated at $91.48 a barrel before the weekend — further strikes could push energy costs higher globally, which means more expensive fuel and goods for everyday Australians. Trump is also reported to be planning 'something much bigger' for the Middle East, raising fears the conflict could widen significantly.

stories.title: Trump courts Supreme Court to allow mail-in voting restrictions ahead of US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Federal judges have now twice blocked the Trump administration's attempt to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the US midterm elections. The administration has escalated to the Supreme Court, asking it to allow the new rules to take effect. At the heart of it: the Trump team wants to limit who can vote by mail and tighten ID requirements, which critics say will suppress turnout. With ballots already going out in some states, the outcome of this Supreme Court battle could shape the midterm results — and by extension, the direction of US policy.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran war 'small potatoes' — hints at larger Middle East strategy
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump publicly described the ongoing US-Iran war as 'small potatoes', suggesting his administration views it as a manageable sideshow rather than the primary focus. Multiple reports say Trump is working on a much larger Middle East plan — details are unclear but analysts suggest it could involve broader military or diplomatic action targeting Iran or reshaping regional alliances. If this escalates, it has serious implications for oil supply, global inflation, and financial market stability — all of which affect Australian investors and consumers.

markets.summary: Last night the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both dipped modestly — less than 0.4% — in a cautious end-of-week session. Tech was the weakest spot, with Microsoft and Google both falling. The ASX 200 closed today down just 0.16%, essentially flat. Oil nudged higher to $91.48 on Middle East tension, while gold slipped slightly. The Aussie dollar was steady at 72.05 US cents.

politics.summary: The Albanese government is pushing new social media regulation with massive fines, the RBA is flagging that rents are keeping inflation sticky, and veterans groups are hitting out at the government over entitlements.

stories.title: Albanese government proposes $100 million fines for social media companies directing users to harmful content
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is proposing legislation that would hit social media platforms with fines of up to $100 million if their algorithms direct users toward harmful content. This is a significant step beyond the existing under-16 social media ban — it targets the recommendation systems that push content to all users, not just kids. For everyday Australians, it could mean platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Instagram have to dramatically change how they serve content. For tech investors, it signals Australia is getting more serious about platform regulation.

stories.title: RBA warns rent prices are keeping inflation stubborn — rate hike fears rising
stories.why_it_matters: The RBA has flagged that stubbornly high rent prices are one of the key reasons inflation isn't falling fast enough in Australia. With rents rising sharply in most capital cities, the bank is reluctant to cut rates — because cheaper money would likely push property demand (and rents) even higher. For renters, this is a double blow: high rents AND interest rates staying higher for longer. For mortgage holders, the message is 'don't expect rate relief anytime soon'.

stories.title: Australia heading into a 'new interest rate reality' — what it means for borrowers
stories.why_it_matters: New analysis suggests Australia is entering a period where interest rates will stay higher for longer than most people expected — and that the shift will be 'significant'. Two key drivers: persistent rent inflation (flagged by the RBA) and global rate trends driven by the US Federal Reserve's cautious approach. For Australians with mortgages or variable-rate debt, this means higher repayments persisting well into 2027. It also changes the calculus for property buyers hoping for a rate-cut windfall.

stories.title: Veterans groups slam Albanese government over entitlements treatment
stories.why_it_matters: A Canberra Daily opinion piece is accusing the Albanese government of 'appalling treatment' of Australian veterans, alleging delays and inadequate support for entitlements claims. The article doesn't detail specific policy changes but suggests systemic failures in the DVA (Department of Veterans' Affairs) processing. With a federal election still in the frame, veteran welfare is likely to become a political flashpoint — particularly in electorates with large defence communities.

ai.summary: A massive week for AI: OpenAI dropped GPT-6 Astra today, all four major AI labs released new models, and the debate over how to regulate autonomous AI agents is intensifying at a global level.

stories.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Astra — a new generation of intelligence
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI published details on GPT-6 Astra today — its latest and most powerful model. While full benchmarks weren't in the headlines, the release signals OpenAI is maintaining its lead in the AI race against Google, Anthropic and Meta. For your GXAI.AX ETF, which holds AI-related companies, a new frontier model keeps the hype and investment cycle running. Practically, GPT-6 Astra will likely unlock more capable AI assistants, coding tools, and business automation in the coming months.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta all ship new AI models — with the same catch
stories.why_it_matters: All four of the world's top AI labs — OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google (Gemini), and Meta — released new models around the same time this week. The 'same catch' reportedly refers to the fact that while each claims breakthroughs, real-world performance differences between the top models are increasingly narrow. Translation: the AI arms race is getting more competitive and expensive, but it's harder for any one company to claim a decisive lead. Good news for users (more choice, lower prices), mixed news for investors betting on a single winner.

stories.title: Rogue AI agents are no longer theoretical — calls for urgent global regulation
stories.why_it_matters: AI 'agents' — programs that can take actions autonomously (browse the web, send emails, book things, write code) — are now real and being deployed at scale. Experts are warning that 'rogue agents' that behave in unexpected or harmful ways are no longer a science-fiction concern, they're a live risk. The article argues governments must regulate agentic AI now, before incidents become widespread. For everyday people, this matters because AI agents are increasingly embedded in tools they use at work and home — and the guardrails are still being figured out.

stories.title: G20 debates AI regulation — US wants minimal rules, others push back
stories.why_it_matters: At G20 discussions, the US is pushing for a 'light-touch' approach to AI regulation — essentially, let the industry self-regulate and innovate freely. Other nations, particularly in Europe, are pushing for stronger rules. Meanwhile, the backlash against massive AI data centre energy consumption is growing, and the US-China rivalry over AI dominance is intensifying. For investors in AI-linked stocks, less regulation is generally seen as a short-term positive for US tech companies like Google and Microsoft.

sport.summary: NRL Round 27 is wrapping up with some big results — Raiders smashed the Cowboys, Rabbitohs put 50 on the Roosters, and the Panthers are currently putting away the Tigers. In AFL, the finals are underway with Sydney and Brisbane shaping as the teams to beat.

stories.title: Raiders demolish Cowboys 50-30 in Townsville
stories.why_it_matters: The Canberra Raiders ran riot in Townsville, beating the North Queensland Cowboys 50-30 in a statement performance. The Raiders look serious finals contenders heading into the back end of the regular season. A 20-point road win over a Cowboys side at home is no fluke — Canberra's attack was relentless.

stories.title: Rabbitohs demolish Roosters 50-20 in the Sydney Derby
stories.why_it_matters: South Sydney put 50 points on the Sydney Roosters on Friday night at Allianz Stadium — a 50-20 drubbing in one of the season's biggest derby performances. The Rabbitohs look like a genuine finals threat, while the Roosters will be deeply concerned about their defensive shape heading into the pointy end of the season.

stories.title: Melbourne Storm beat Cronulla Sharks 24-20 in a late comeback
stories.why_it_matters: Melbourne Storm pulled off a late miracle to beat the Cronulla Sharks 24-20 in what the Telegraph described as a fitting end to a troubled Storm season. Despite off-field issues throughout 2026, the Storm's never-say-die character showed again at Ocean Protect Stadium on Saturday night. The result keeps their finals hopes alive.

stories.title: AFL Finals: Geelong stun in comeback, Dangerfield moment goes viral
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong pulled off a stunning finals comeback that has AFL Twitter going wild. Patrick Dangerfield was at the centre of a moment described as 'historic' — though details of the specific act weren't in the article text, the reaction suggests it was extraordinary sportsmanship or skill. Sydney and Brisbane are still rated the finals favourites based on the player ratings doing the rounds, but Geelong's revival adds a third genuine contender to the premiership race.
